properties.description: Drop the staged base64 payload for an image whose decoded bytes are now persisted in the render cache; see [`register_payload`].

properties.name: restage_requested_payloads
properties.description: Rare recovery path for payloads removed by the staging byte budget or an image visibility toggle. The steady-state fast path is one relaxed atomic load; only an actual miss clones/scans the App's image list.

properties.name: materialize_visible
properties.description: Ensure the image with `id` is materialized (decoded + cached) so it can be drawn. Returns true on success. Steady-state frames hit a cheap in-memory presence probe (no payload clone, no payload hash); only the first visible frame for an image pays the decode + cache cost.

properties.name: ensure_drawable
properties.description: Make sure image `id` can be drawn cheaply this frame. Returns true when the draw path can run now without heavy work (image decoded and, on Kitty, scale+transmit state matches the placeholder geometry). Returns false after scheduling background preparation; the caller should skip drawing this frame and rely on the completion nudge to repaint.

properties.name: prefetch
properties.description: Warm an inline image that is *not* on screen yet so it is ready to draw the instant it scrolls into view. Unlike [`ensure_drawable`], this never blocks and never draws: if the image still needs decode/scale/transmit work it is scheduled on the background prewarm worker (deduped against in-flight and already-warm state), otherwise it is a cheap no-op. Callers pass the same `(target_cols, target_rows)` placeholder geometry the draw path will use, so the prewarmed Kitty fit-state matches exactly and the first on-screen frame hits the `Ready` fast path with no rescale.

properties.name: unplaced_items
properties.description: Items that will NOT be placed inside the transcript body: unanchored images plus anchored images whose anchor target does not exist among `messages` (e.g. live images for a tool whose transcript entry was replaced). These fall back to the bottom inline-images section so no image ever silently disappears.

properties.name: AnchoredCacheKey
properties.description: One-slot cache for [`resolve_anchored_items`], keyed by the image-set signature. Resolving hashes every image payload (for ids), so body preparation must not redo it per rebuild; the signature is already cached per transcript version on the app side.

properties.name: resolve_anchored_items_cached
properties.description: Resolve the app's images into anchored buckets, cached by the image-set signature. Returns an empty result without touching payloads when the app has no images or inline images are hidden.

properties.name: fit_geometry_with_cap
properties.description: Compute how many `(rows, cols)` an inline image occupies at `chat_width`, capped at `cap_rows`. `cols` includes the 2-cell left border, matching what the draw step actually paints, so layout (e.g. info widget placement) can know the real horizontal extent.

properties.name: fit_geometry
properties.description: Compute `(rows, cols)` for an inline image at `chat_width`, given a viewport height to cap against.

properties.name: fit_geometry_anchored
properties.description: Compute `(rows, cols)` for an image anchored inside the transcript body at a given expand level. Uses a fixed (viewport-independent) row cap so the body's prepared lines stay valid across resizes (the body cache is keyed by width only); the expand level only swaps which fixed cap applies.

properties.name: image_label_line
properties.description: Build the dim label line shown above an inline image, e.g. ` screenshot.png 1920×1080`, with a trailing show/hide badge (`[Alt] [⇧] [I] hide` / `[Alt] [⇧] [I] show image`) so the toggle is discoverable right where the image renders. The line is kept deliberately short so it fits on one row; there is no visible expand badge, but clicking the rendered image body still cycles the per-image size (see `inline_image_body_target_from_screen`).

properties.name: anchored_image_lines
properties.description: Lines for images anchored at a transcript message: per image, a leading blank, a dim label, a geometry-encoding marker line plus blank placeholder rows (recognized by the image-region scan), and a trailing blank. When `images_visible` is false the image collapses to just its label stub (with a `show image` badge) and no placeholder rows are emitted, so nothing is painted.

properties.name: build_section
properties.description: Build the inline-images prepared section: a heading + correctly-sized placeholder per image, with explicit `image_regions` (render = Fit) that the viewport draws lazily. When `images_visible` is false each image collapses to its label stub and no regions are emitted.

properties.name: materialize_with_retry
properties.description: Materialize `id`, retrying against unrelated parallel tests that wipe the process-global image state (`mermaid::clear_image_state()` runs on diagram geometry changes, zoom, and session-picker paths). Each retry re-stages the payload because `register_payload` is skipped while an image is materialized and a wipe can clear both stores at once.

properties.name: picker_entry_pretty_name
properties.description: Human-friendly rendering of a model picker row's model name. `/model` rows historically showed the raw provider model id (`claude-opus-4-8`, `gpt-5.5 (high)`), which reads worse than the pretty names every other surface uses (header, status line, info widgets). We prettify only the well-known families so unfamiliar or namespaced ids (OpenRouter `vendor/model`, local profiles) keep their exact spelling and stay copy-pasteable. Effort suffixes such as ` (high)` are preserved.

properties.name: command_suggestions_overlay_rect
properties.description: Where the command-suggestion popover should render, given the input chunk. Suggestions are an overlay: they never participate in the vertical layout, so opening the palette never moves the transcript, the status line, or the pinned footer. Preferred position is directly below the input (over blank rows / the pinned footer); when the input sits at the bottom of the screen the popover flips above the input, covering the last transcript rows instead of reflowing them.

properties.name: command_suggestions_active
properties.description: Whether the command palette is active for the current composer state.

properties.name: draw_prompt_history_search_overlay
properties.description: Draw the Ctrl+R reverse prompt-history search overlay. Reuses the command-palette positioning: floats below (or above) the input without reserving layout height. Shows the query line plus the match list with the selected row highlighted.

properties.name: draw_command_suggestions_overlay
properties.description: Draw the command-suggestion popover as a late overlay pass. Called after the chunked layout (and info widgets) have rendered so the palette floats over existing rows instead of reserving layout height.

properties.name: command_suggestion_needle
properties.description: Extract the slash-command portion of the typed input that should be matched against suggestion command tokens for highlighting purposes.

properties.name: highlight_command_spans
properties.description: Build spans for a suggestion command, recoloring the characters that the fuzzy matcher aligned with the typed query. Falls back to a single unhighlighted span when there is nothing (useful) to highlight.

properties.name: brighten_command_color
properties.description: Blend a palette color toward white to emphasize a matched character while keeping its original hue.

properties.name: dim_command_color
properties.description: Blend a palette color toward black so unmatched characters recede.

properties.name: push_queued_suffix
properties.description: Append the "+N queued" suffix span (in the queued accent color) when there are queued follow-up messages. Centralizes the repeated check/styling shared by every processing-status branch in `draw_status`.

properties.name: build_notification_spans
properties.description: Build the spans for the notification line. Returns empty vec when there is nothing to show. This is the single source of truth for notification content - both the layout height calculation (via `has_notification`) and the renderer call this.

properties.name: draw_overscroll_status
properties.description: Draw the elastic overscroll status line, revealed below the input when the user scrolls past the bottom of the transcript. Shows model, provider, access method, reasoning level, and context usage percentage, with a live `(overscroll x.x)` countdown pinned to the right so users can see the line is temporary and rebounds away on its own.

properties.name: overscroll_truncate_spans
properties.description: Truncate a list of spans to at most `max_width` display columns, appending a single-cell ellipsis when content is dropped. Preserves per-span styling.

properties.name: overscroll_git_branch
properties.description: Format a working dir path home-relative (~/foo/bar), keeping the last 2 segments. Compact git branch label for the status line and fact stack. Truncated so long branch names cannot crowd out the other facts.

properties.name: overscroll_is_placeholder
properties.description: Placeholder header strings used during remote startup; not real model names.

properties.name: overscroll_is_runtime_placeholder
properties.description: Inert runtime provider labels (remote/replay/test-harness) shown before the real provider name is known; not real provider names.

properties.name: overscroll_context_bar
properties.description: Render a compact rounded progress bar (◖████░░◗) plus a percentage label.

properties.name: right_fact_lines
properties.description: Build fact rows in their visual top-to-bottom order: provider/auth, model, directory, then context usage. Placement walks this list in reverse so the context row is anchored nearest the input whenever space permits.

properties.name: input_copy_snapshot_parts
properties.description: Wrapped/raw text plus the wrapped-to-raw line map for the composer's copy-selection snapshot. Wrapped rows mirror `wrap_input_segments` exactly (the same function that lays out the rendered rows), while raw lines are the logical `\n`-separated input lines, so copying a selection that spans a soft wrap yields the original text without injected line breaks.

properties.name: composer_line_width
properties.description: The usable text width of one composer row, i.e. the width used by `wrap_input_segments` when the composer is rendered into `area_width`. Returns `None` when there is no room for text.

properties.name: visual_line_move
properties.description: Move the cursor one *visual* (wrapped) row up (`delta = -1`) or down (`delta = 1`) within the composer, keeping the display column. Returns the new byte offset, or `None` when the cursor is already on the first/last visual row (so callers can fall through to prompt history).

properties.name: split_plan_segments
properties.description: Split assistant content into markdown/plan segments when it contains at least one ```plan fenced block. Returns `None` when there is no plan block so the common path stays on the plain markdown renderer.

properties.name: render_plan_card
properties.description: Render the inner markdown of a ```plan block as a bordered plan card.

properties.name: plan_card_title
properties.description: Title for the plan card: the first markdown heading in the body, else "Plan".

properties.name: plan_card_body_without_title
properties.description: Remove the first heading line when it was promoted to the card title.

properties.name: render_reasoning_message
properties.description: Render a collapsed/collapsing reasoning trace ("current" mode). The content is sentinel-wrapped dim+italic markup (reasoning lines and/or a `▸ thought for Xs` summary), so it reuses the standard markdown path that styles those runs dim.

properties.name: render_plaintext_lines
properties.description: Wrap plaintext content into lines without any markdown interpretation. System messages are status/notice text and must render verbatim (no bold, headings, list bullets, code fences, etc.). This word-wraps on whitespace and hard-splits tokens that are wider than `wrap_width`, preserving the author's own line breaks and leading indentation. Wrapped continuation lines are hang-indented to match the original line's indentation so that authored plaintext layout (indented commands, aligned blocks) survives.

properties.name: render_agentgrep_output_body
properties.description: Render the full agentgrep tool output inline beneath the tool summary line. Each output line is prefixed with a dim left border and indented so it reads as a nested block. Long lines are hard-split to the available width and the block is capped so a giant search result cannot flood the transcript.

properties.name: content_has_markdown_formatting
properties.description: Heuristic: does authored system content use markdown formatting that is worth rendering (bold/italic, inline code, headings, lists, links, blockquotes, fenced code, tables)? Plain status/help text (no markdown) keeps the original plaintext path so authored indentation is preserved and long lines wrap to width. We only opt into markdown when a marker is actually present, which avoids regressing indented/aligned output that markdown parsing would otherwise flatten.

properties.name: preserve_hard_line_breaks_for_markdown
properties.description: Convert single newlines in authored system content into markdown hard line breaks (a trailing ` ` before the newline) so the renderer keeps each source line on its own row instead of reflowing them into one paragraph. Blank-line paragraph boundaries are left untouched, and lines that already belong to block constructs (list items, headings, fenced code, blockquotes, tables) are not given a hard break since markdown already breaks on them.

properties.name: render_todos_message
properties.description: Render the inline todo-list card (`role == "todos"`). New payloads contain both todo items and goal assessments; the legacy item-array shape remains supported so older transcript entries keep rendering.

properties.name: push_todo_plan_details
properties.description: Plan-level assessment lines shown once above the todo groups.

properties.name: push_todo_wrapped_detail
properties.description: Wrap one labeled detail line to the card width.

properties.name: render_todo_assessment_updates
properties.description: Concise refinement card for assessment-only todo writes: the plan-level intent change first, then any per-goal quality updates.

properties.name: welcome_accent
properties.description: Accent color for the welcome title.

properties.name: push_esc_skip_hint
properties.description: Append the universal "Esc to skip" hint shown on every guided onboarding phase. This advertises the escape hatch that guarantees the user can always leave onboarding (see `handle_onboarding_continue_prompt_key`), so a first- run user is never visibly trapped. Kept dim and on its own line so it never competes with the primary action.

properties.name: rounded_pill_caps_supported
properties.description: Whether the terminal renders the U+25D6/U+25D7 half-circle pill caps as clean full-cell semicircles. Kitty does; ghostty, Apple Terminal, and the VS Code terminal draw them as small floating glyphs that break the capsule illusion, so those fall back to half-block caps that render solidly everywhere. Override with `JCODE_ROUNDED_PILLS=on|off`.

properties.name: lozenge_pill_spans
properties.description: Build one rounded "lozenge" pill: half-circle end caps (`◖` / `◗`) around a padded label. Both states are solid capsules; the selected pill has a bright accent fill + BOLD label, the unselected one a muted dark-gray fill with no bold. The BOLD-vs-not-bold contrast is a non-color attribute, so the selection survives on monochrome terminals (Tier 10 color-independence).

properties.name: yes_no_pill_line
properties.description: Build the Yes/No selector as a pair of rounded lozenge pills. The selected option is a bright filled pill; the other is a muted dark capsule. The shape and fill carry the selection visually so no instruction sentence is needed.

properties.name: continue_pill_line
properties.description: A rounded "Continue" pill button. Rendered above the import list so the user can reach the commit action just by arrowing up out of the rows (no need to read a "Press Enter" instruction). Uses the same lozenge style as the Yes/No pills: a filled accent capsule when `focused`, a hollow outline otherwise.

properties.name: import_summary_pills_line
properties.description: The summary-screen action row. A new user can import the logins we found or use a blaude subscription, with secondary controls for a selective import and telemetry settings.

properties.name: telemetry_settings_lines
properties.description: The telemetry settings sub-page: three stacked pills, most sharing first, each with a dim one-line consequence caption. Reached from the "Telemetry settings" pill on the import summary; Esc returns without changing anything.

properties.name: import_summary_lines
properties.description: Render the read-only detected-login list for the import summary screen: one dim checkmarked row per detected login. No cursor, no columns - the user is just being shown what we found before they hit Continue.

properties.name: import_two_column_lines
properties.description: Render the import screen body: a "Yes / No" header row, then one row per detected login. Each login has a circle under the Yes column and a circle under the No column; the *filled* circle is the current choice. Every login defaults to "Yes" (import), so the pre-selected state is obvious: the Yes column is already filled. The cursor row is marked with a `>` gutter, and Left/Right move the choice between Yes and No. The header, circles, and gutter are interactive-widget glyphs, not load-bearing prose: the surrounding ASCII copy ("We found N existing logins", "Imports all checked in Ns") already conveys state in plain text.

properties.name: telemetry_header_lines
properties.description: Grayed telemetry notice shown at the very top of the onboarding screen.

properties.name: welcome_title_line
properties.description: Welcome title line, rendered above the phase body.

properties.name: keyboard_hint_line
properties.description: Short keyboard hint rendered on guided phases. Replaces the old multi-line instruction prose: the interactive pills/rows already show what is selectable, so a one-liner is enough.

properties.name: welcome_body_lines
properties.description: The phase-specific body of the welcome screen (everything below the title and keyboard hint), so this no longer emits the title itself.

properties.name: draw_onboarding_welcome
properties.description: Draw the full onboarding welcome screen into `area`. Vertical structure (top to bottom): telemetry header, gap, title, keyboard hint, gap, phase body.

properties.name: collect_pinned_diffs_cached
properties.description: Collect the pinned file-diff entries used by the right-hand pane. Inline images render in the transcript now. Keeping image payloads out of this frame-level probe is important because `TuiState::side_pane_images()` may materialize and clone multi-megabyte base64 strings.

properties.name: assistant_aux_data
properties.description: Compute (and cache) the auxiliary raw-line-map data for an assistant message. `cached` is the already-rendered (and possibly cached) display lines for the message; `align` and `centered` describe the current display mode.

properties.name: compute_image_regions
properties.description: Build the image regions for an image/mermaid placeholder in `wrapped_lines`, where each placeholder "owns" the run of blank lines that follow it. Done in a single reverse pass that precomputes, for every line, the length of the blank run starting at that line. The previous implementation scanned forward through the trailing blanks for every placeholder, which is O(L^2) when a message has many placeholders each followed by long blank runs.

properties.name: todo_change_lines
properties.description: Build the inline "what changed" delta lines for a `todo` tool message, if it is a successful write. `messages` is the full transcript and `abs_idx` is the absolute index of the todo message, so the previous todo list can be found.

properties.name: push_user_prompt_lines
annotations:
#[expect(
    clippy::too_many_arguments,
    reason = "User prompt rendering updates the prepared-line side tables together"
)]

properties.name: stamp_mermaid_pending
properties.description: Stamp `prepared` with the deferred-mermaid staleness marker: `Some(epoch)` when any wrapped line is the "rendering mermaid diagram..." placeholder (a background render is still in flight), `None` otherwise. `epoch_before` must be the deferred-render epoch read *before* the markdown was rendered, so a render completing mid-build immediately reads as stale.

properties.name: merge_mermaid_pending
properties.description: Merge the pending stamp of a reused base with a freshly rendered part. Keeps the earliest epoch so staleness is never masked.

properties.name: first_mermaid_pending_message
properties.description: Transcript message index owning the first deferred-mermaid pending placeholder line, for cutting a stale base at a message boundary. `None` when no pending line exists.

properties.name: initial_header_pad_top
properties.description: Top padding used to vertically center the header on the initial empty screen. Derived only from the persistent header height (not suggestions) so the same value can be re-applied above the header once messages exist, keeping the header from jumping when the first prompt is sent.

properties.name: build_top_pad_lines
properties.description: Build the lines that fill the top padding above the header. Unseen release notes (the "Updates" box) render inside this padding, bottom-aligned so any leftover space stays at the top. With no unseen updates this is just blank padding. The returned vec is always exactly `pad_top` lines tall so the header position never shifts.

properties.name: invalidate_header_prep_cache
properties.description: Drop the prepared-header cache so the next frame re-probes the disk-backed surfaces (auth inventory, skills, goal badge, update badges). The TTL alone is sized for background drift. Actions taken *inside* the TUI that change those surfaces - completing `/login`, adding an account, reloading skills - must be reflected immediately rather than up to a full TTL later, so they call this directly.

properties.name: header_prep_signature
properties.description: Hash of the header inputs that are cheap to read every frame. Anything expensive (disk probes) is intentionally excluded and covered by the TTL.

properties.name: build_body_from_base
properties.description: Rebuild the body reusing as much of a cached base as possible. Tries, in order: exact reuse (identical messages), suffix reuse (older history was prepended above an otherwise unchanged transcript - the "scroll to top of a compacted session" path), and prefix reuse (append / tail edit). Falls back to re-rendering whatever cannot be reused.

properties.name: BodyRenderCtx
properties.description: Immutable per-build render context shared by the full and incremental body builders. Holding this in one place keeps the single per-message renderer (`render_message_into`) free of divergence between the two entry points.

properties.name: push_auto
properties.description: Push a fully-rendered display line whose raw selection text is the line itself (no logical-line mapping). Seeds a contiguous raw entry and an explicit full-width override so the body's `raw_plain_lines` stays message-ordered. Keeping raws contiguous is what lets a tail-edit rebuild truncate both the wrapped arrays *and* the raw array at a message boundary, avoiding an unbounded raw leak across repeated tail edits (e.g. a streaming tool result that updates many times).

properties.name: push_blank
properties.description: Push a blank separator line. Routed through `push_auto` so it seeds a (empty) raw and keeps the raw array contiguous.

properties.name: render_message_into
properties.description: Render a single transcript message into `acc`. This is the one canonical per-message renderer; the full and incremental body builders both call it so their output cannot drift (which previously caused subtle text-selection and spacing differences on the incremental path).

properties.name: truncate_prepared_to_boundary
properties.description: Truncate a prepared body so it contains exactly the first `keep_msgs` messages, in place on the (uniquely owned) `prepared`. Used by prefix reuse: when an incoming rebuild shares a hash prefix of length `keep_msgs` with a cached body, the body is truncated here and the changed tail is re-appended via `prepare_body_incremental`. The cut always lands on a message boundary, so every wrapped-indexed entry belongs entirely to either the kept prefix or the dropped tail; filtering by `start < wrapped_len` is exact. Requires message-contiguous raws (guaranteed by the shared body renderer), which lets the raw array be truncated too rather than leaked.

properties.name: matching_prefix_len
properties.description: Longest message prefix length `k` such that `base.message_boundaries[..k]` hashes match the first `k` messages of `messages`. Returns `0` when nothing matches (caller then does a full rebuild). Bounded by the shorter of the two lengths.

properties.name: matching_suffix_len
properties.description: Longest message suffix length `s` such that the last `s` boundaries of `base` hash-match the last `s` entries of `messages`. Used to detect a prepend (older compacted history loaded above an unchanged tail).

properties.name: suffix_reuse_compatible
properties.description: Whether a cached body whose message suffix matches the current transcript can be reused verbatim below a freshly rendered head. The reused lines bake in per-prompt state, so this verifies that state is invariant under the prepend: - Displayed prompt numbers: the base rendered `local_num + base_offset`; a full rebuild renders `new_local_num + current_offset`. They agree exactly when `dropped_prompts + base_offset == head_prompts + current_offset` (loading compacted history reveals prompts, decreasing the hidden-prompt offset by the same amount, so this holds in the real flow). - Prompt-anchored inline images embed window-relative prompt ordinals that all shift under a prepend, so any `by_prompt` anchors force a rebuild. Rainbow prompt-number colors and todo "what changed" deltas may be slightly stale in the reused suffix (they can depend on messages outside it). Both are cosmetic, match the existing staleness of the append/prefix-reuse path, and self-correct on any full rebuild (e.g. a width change).

properties.name: prepare_body_prepended
properties.description: Rebuild a body as `freshly rendered head + reused suffix of a cached base`, in place on `prev`. This is the prepend analogue of [`prepare_body_incremental`]: when older compacted history is loaded above an unchanged tail, only the new head (marker + revealed messages) is rendered and wrapped; the prepared suffix is kept and its line/raw indices are shifted. Returns `Err(prev)` untouched when the stitch would not be sound so the caller can fall back to the prefix/full paths.

properties.name: wrap_lines_with_map
annotations:
#[expect(
    clippy::too_many_arguments,
    reason = "Wrapped-line preparation carries explicit render state to avoid hidden coupling"
)]

properties.name: hash_row
properties.description: Hash one buffer row's cell symbols within `area`. Returns [`BLANK_ROW_HASH`] for visually blank rows.

properties.name: frame_from_buffer
properties.description: Build an [`AnchorFrame`] from a rendered buffer region. Shared by the live recorder hook and offscreen benchmark tests (which feed frames into their own local [`AnchorStabilityRecorder`] for deterministic assertions).

properties.name: observe_frame
properties.description: Observe the rendered messages area for this frame. Called once per draw.

properties.name: report_json
properties.description: Pretty JSON anchor-stability report for the debug socket.

properties.name: reset
properties.description: Reset the recorder (e.g. to measure one turn or one replay in isolation).

properties.name: semver
properties.description: Extract semantic version for UI display/grouping.

properties.name: is_running_stable_release
properties.description: True when this process is running from the stable release binary path. Only matches the explicit ~/.jcode/builds/stable/jcode path, NOT ~/.local/bin/jcode launcher path (which now points to current).

properties.name: assert_prepared_equivalent
properties.description: Assert two prepared bodies are byte-for-byte equivalent across every observable array. Used to prove prefix-reuse output matches a fresh full build.

properties.name: pin_full_tier
properties.description: Pin the performance tier before reading any redraw policy. `redraw_interval` and `periodic_redraw_required` consult `perf::tui_policy()`, and the auto-detected tier depends on host load: under a parallel cargo build the host can look Reduced/Minimal, where the decorative animation is legitimately disabled. `pin_full_profile_for_tests` is first-initialization-wins, so a test that reads the policy without pinning inherits whatever another test happened to establish. That is exactly how these tests flaked once in a full parallel suite while passing in isolation.

properties.name: IdleAnimationEnvGuard
properties.description: RAII guard enabling `display.idle_animation` for one test. The decorative idle donut is opt-in since 17e075fb2 flipped the config default to `false`, but these tests exist to pin the donut's redraw cadence and partial-repaint machinery, which only run when the feature is on. Holds the shared test-env lock for its lifetime so the env mutation cannot leak into tests that expect the default-off behavior. Acquire this guard *before* any render-state lock, matching the env-then-render order the app tests use.

properties.name: static_chrome_state
properties.description: A state whose only "live" element is a piece of static text chrome.

properties.name: just_touched_notice_screen
properties.description: The post-onboarding notice screen: the transcript holds only system notices ("Here are a few things you can try", the login summary), the user pressed a key moments ago, and no stream has ever run in this process. `time_since_activity()` reports "past the deep-idle threshold" for any non-empty never-streamed transcript, which is meant for *restored dormant* sessions. Treating this screen as dormant parked the donut and the redraw loop at the 5s crawl the instant onboarding finished, so the decorative animation never ran on the exact screen it was designed for. A recent keystroke is proof the session is not dormant.

properties.name: render_inline_picker
properties.description: Render the inline interactive picker for the given state and return the per-row text of the whole buffer.

properties.name: viewport_snapshot_test_lock
properties.description: Delegates to the single shared render-state lock so viewport-snapshot tests serialize against every other rendering test, not just each other (#593).

properties.name: render_onboarding
properties.description: Render the onboarding welcome screen for the given state at the given size and return the flattened text of the whole buffer.

properties.name: measure
properties.description: Render a set of representative frames and tally role area plus adjacency.
properties.returnType:
(
    BTreeMap<&'static str, u32>,
    BTreeMap<(&'static str, &'static str), u32>,
)

properties.name: buffer_rows
properties.description: Buffer contents as one string per row (not trimmed, full width).

properties.name: todos_from_tool_input
properties.description: Parse the todo list a `todo` tool call wrote. Returns `None` for read calls (no `todos` argument) or when the payload cannot be parsed for display.

properties.name: previous_todos
properties.description: Find the todo list written by the most recent `todo` tool message before `current_abs_idx`. Skips read-only todo calls so a write's delta is computed against the previous *write*.

properties.name: is_substantive
properties.description: Form B (multi-line block) vs Form A (one line). Substantive changes get the block; minor tweaks collapse to a single summary line.

properties.name: change_marker
properties.description: Leading marker (glyph + color) and the text color used for a change line.

properties.name: render_todo_change_lines
properties.description: Build the delta lines to inject below a `todo` tool message. Returns an empty vec when nothing meaningful changed (reads, no-op writes).

properties.name: get_tool_summary
properties.description: Extract a brief summary from a tool call input (file path, command, etc.)

properties.name: get_tool_activity_detail
properties.description: Detail text for the live activity line while a tool is running. Prefers the model-provided `intent` (display-only description of why the call is being made) and appends the technical summary when it adds information.

properties.name: batch_subcall_params

properties.name: source_files
properties.description: Map of relative path -> file text for every .swift under source_root.

properties.name: fitts_time
properties.description: Fitts' law touch movement time in seconds: ``a + b * log2(D/W + 1)``. ``distance_pt`` is the travel distance D (pt); ``target_w_pt`` is the effective target width W (pt). W is guarded to be > 0; non-positive widths are clamped to a tiny epsilon so the log stays finite (treated as a very hard target). Negative distances are clamped to 0.

properties.name: _effective_width
properties.description: W along the movement axis (see module docstring: conservative proxy).

properties.name: action_cost
properties.description: Price one ``Action`` in seconds with a per-operator + Fitts + response breakdown. Sums operator times for ``action.operators``, adds a Fitts movement time for each TAP that acquires ``action.target_id`` (from the previous thumb position), adds ``action.response_s``, and applies a large penalty if the action's target has ``exists=False``. Returns a ``CostBreakdown`` whose ``detail`` aggregates per-operator seconds plus ``'fitts'`` and ``'response'`` (and ``'unknown_ops'`` / ``'unreachable'`` when relevant).

properties.name: _targets_for_action
properties.description: Return targets with the action's OWN target forced present. Some controls are context-conditional (e.g. the composer 'stop' button only appears while a turn is running). The ui_map marks those exists=False, but when the user performs the action that uses them, they are by definition on screen. Forcing just this action's target present avoids a spurious 'unreachable' penalty while still flagging genuinely missing controls.

properties.name: _stationary_distribution
properties.description: Power-iterate the state-transition matrix to its stationary distribution. Transition prob from s = sum over out-edges to dst of normalized weight. Self-loops (chat->chat actions like send/scroll) keep mass in that state, correctly making 'chat' dominant since that is where most actions happen.

properties.name: reward_score
properties.description: Map the engine's expected per-action cost to a 0..100 reward.

properties.name: _default_profile
properties.description: Build a literature-default profile so the engine runs on a fresh machine.

properties.name: _normalize
properties.description: Return weights normalized to sum 1.0 (stable order = MOBILE_ACTIONS).

properties.name: _select_log_files
properties.description: Return up to `days` (date, path) pairs, most recent first, by filename date.

properties.name: _scan_file
properties.description: Stream one log file line-by-line, accumulating into `counts`. Returns the number of lines scanned. Cheap substring guards keep the hot loop fast on 100k+ line files; only candidate lines are parsed further.

properties.name: _map_to_mobile
properties.description: Map mined raw TUI counts onto the OBSERVED mobile actions.

properties.name: mine_usage
properties.description: Mine the last `days` daily logs under `log_dir` into a :class:`UsageProfile`. Degrades gracefully: if the directory is absent, empty, or contains no user-action markers, returns a literature-default profile so the engine still runs on a fresh machine / in CI.

properties.name: _read_sources
properties.description: Read the Swift view files; missing files map to '' (defaults kick in).

properties.name: _image_frames
properties.description: Map each ``Image(systemName:)`` to the first ``.frame(width:height:)`` that follows it (before the next image), i.e. the icon's explicit size from source.

properties.name: _pad_after
properties.description: First ``.padding(.{axis}, N)`` after ``anchor``; else ``default``.

properties.name: _pad_all_after
properties.description: First ``.padding(N)`` (all-edges) after ``anchor``; else ``default``.

properties.name: _size_from_source
properties.description: Return the parsed (w, h) for an icon, or the HIG-min fallback + a note.

properties.name: _pairing_targets

properties.name: _default_source_root
properties.description: <repo>/ios/Sources/JCodeMobile, resolved relative to this file.

properties.name: build_ui_map
properties.description: Build the per-screen map of tappable-control geometry from the Swift source. Returns a dict keyed by screen/state id -- ``"chat"``, ``"settings_sheet"``, ``"pairing"`` -- each a list of :class:`UITarget` (center + size in points). Conditionally-shown controls (e.g. the composer stop button) are included with ``exists=False`` so the cost model can price both states. Size assumptions are recorded in :data:`LAYOUT_ASSUMPTIONS` (also via :func:`assumptions`).

properties.name: assumptions
properties.description: Return the assumption/provenance notes from the most recent build.

properties.name: _largest_color_component
properties.description: Bounding box (x0, y0, x1, y1) of the largest 4-connected True region. Pure-NumPy flood fill; deterministic. Returns None if the mask is empty.

properties.name: best
properties.declaredType: tuple[int, tuple[int, int, int, int]] | None

properties.name: build_ui_map_from_screenshot
properties.description: Measure control geometry from a real screenshot (deterministic). Detects the dominant ``Theme.mint`` blob (the send button's filled circle) by color thresholding and returns its measured center + size, converting pixels to points via ``/ scale`` (simulator screenshots are typically @3x). This is a pixel-measured complement to :func:`build_ui_map`; it returns ``{"chat": [UITarget("send_measured", ...)]}`` (empty if no mint blob is found). Requires NumPy + PIL. Use it on screenshots under ``/tmp/jcode-ui-matrix/``.

properties.name: _self_test
properties.description: Lightweight, deterministic invariants (source-based + synthetic screenshot).

properties.name: _flatten_targets
properties.description: All targets keyed by id (ids are unique across screens in ui_map).

properties.name: build_user_model
properties.description: Return (graph, flat_targets, meta). meta carries the usage source + raw mined weights so callers can audit how the edge weights were grounded.

properties.name: _icononly_buttons_without_label
properties.description: Count buttons whose visible content is an SF Symbol with no text/label. Heuristic: for each `Button`, inspect a forward window up to the next `Button` (bounded). If it contains an Image(systemName:) but no Text(), Label(), or .accessibilityLabel, it is an unlabeled icon-only button.

properties.name: _penalty
properties.description: count over the free allowance, times per-hit weight, clamped to the cap.

properties.name: _rgb_to_hsv
properties.description: RGB in 0..255 -> (hue degrees, saturation 0..1, value 0..1).

properties.name: _is_slop_color
properties.description: A vivid purple/indigo or neon-cyan accent (mint #4DD9A6 fails this).

properties.name: _purple_pixel_frac
properties.description: Fraction of vivid content pixels in the purple/indigo or neon-cyan band.

properties.name: _gradient_region_frac
properties.description: Fraction of a coarse block grid covered by smooth multi-stop color ramps. A gradient region is a run of adjacent blocks whose mean color changes by a small, steady step in a consistent direction across many blocks (a smooth ramp), accumulating a large total color distance. Solid tokenized surfaces (zero step) and hard edges (large jumps) do not qualify, so our flat app reads ~0.

properties.name: mark_runs
properties.description: Flag maximal runs of >=6 blocks of small, steady step that together span a large total color distance (a smooth multi-stop ramp). Decorative AI-slop gradients are *colorful* (purple->blue); a grayscale brightness ramp (e.g. anti-aliased mono text over a dark panel) is not a slop gradient, so require real chroma somewhere along the run.

properties.name: _dominant_colors
properties.description: Count quantized colour buckets covering >0.4% of content pixels.

properties.name: _margin_groups
properties.description: Distinct clusters of per-row leftmost content edges (>2% of rows each).

properties.name: _source_hits
properties.description: Count raw colour + raw font literals outside Theme.swift.

properties.name: _relative_luminance
properties.description: sRGB relative luminance per WCAG 2.x. Accepts (...,3) in 0..255.

properties.name: _contrast_ratio
properties.description: WCAG contrast ratio between two relative luminances.

properties.name: _ramp
properties.description: Map a contrast ratio onto 0..100: 1:1 -> 0, >=7:1 (AAA) -> 100.

properties.name: _score_empty_state
properties.description: Empty scenario: grade chrome leanness, not transcript density.

properties.name: _saturating
properties.description: 100 at/below `tol`, 0 at/above `ceiling`, linear in between.

properties.name: _ramp
properties.description: 100 at `good`, 0 at `bad`, linear + clamped. Works for good<bad ramps.

properties.name: _matching_brace
properties.description: Index of the brace matching the `{` at open_idx (or len(text)).

properties.name: _view_bodies
properties.description: (struct_name, struct_body_text) for every `struct X: View`, deterministic.

properties.name: _container_depth
properties.description: Max simultaneously-open layout containers (approx UI nesting depth). Token scan: a container keyword arms `pending`; the next `{` opens a container frame. Other `{` (closures like Button { } / .onChange { }) open non-container frames so they never inflate structural depth.

properties.name: _cardincard
properties.description: Count card regions nested inside another card region. A frame is a "card" if its `{` was a `Card {` opener, or if the current scope carries a `.clipShape(RoundedRectangle)` surface modifier. Opening a second card while an ancestor card frame is still open is the card-in-card slop tell. This is lexical (an approximation): it fires on real nesting like `Card { ... Card { ... } }` and stays at 0 for a flat, disciplined app.

properties.name: _modifier_density
properties.description: Average chained modifiers per element across all views. Modifiers in this codebase sit one-per-line, so counting `^\\s*.\\w+(` lines is a faithful chain length; dividing by element count normalizes for screen size. Long chains per element read as fiddly, incidental complexity.

properties.name: _pixel_regions
properties.description: (total_regions, small_competing_regions) via coarse connected components. Counting raw connected pixels would split every glyph into its own region; that measures text, not layout. Instead we downsample the content mask onto an 8pt grid (one coarse cell per `8*scale` px), mark a cell ON when it is meaningfully covered, then label 4-connected blobs deterministically. Each blob is a visual "block" (a message bubble, a card, the composer). Large, well-separated blocks read as simple; many TINY competing blobs (status dots, scattered chips/badges) are the visual form of "too many primitives", so we report them separately as the thing to penalize.

properties.name: _score_empty_state
properties.description: Empty scenario: a calm canvas with a clear affordance to start. Users landing on an empty chat need exactly one thing: an obvious place to type. Reward (a) a visible composer/affordance in the bottom band, and (b) a fill ratio inside the calm empty-state band. No dead-zone penalty: an empty transcript IS a dead zone by design.

properties.name: _base_hue
properties.description: Hue in degrees for an RGB triple, or None for a greyscale colour.

properties.name: _hsv
properties.description: Vectorized HSV (hue degrees, sat 0..1, val 0..1) for an HxWx3 image.

properties.name: _band
properties.description: 100 inside [lo, hi]; linear ramp to 0 at floor_at (below) / ceil_at (above).

properties.name: _accent_palette
properties.description: Usage count per distinct accent family referenced outside Theme.swift. Chromatic Theme tokens collapse to a family (mintTint -> mint); inline Color(hex:) literals bucket by hue (15 deg buckets) so two near-identical custom colours are not double-counted as a "rainbow".

properties.name: _type_scale
properties.description: (distinct deliberate sizes, distinct semantic roles, distinct weights).

properties.name: _blobs
properties.description: 4-connected components of a boolean mask via scanline run union-find. Returns [(x0, y0, x1, y1, area)] in mask coordinates. Deterministic: the output is sorted by (y0, x0). Fast enough for the thin bands we scan.

properties.name: _band_controls
properties.description: Detect compact control candidates in one full-image band. Returns list of dicts with full-image pixel bbox + point size. y0/y1 are in full-image coordinates (band offset added) so spacing can be measured across bands.

properties.name: _rect_gap_pt
properties.description: Minimum edge-to-edge gap between two bboxes, in points (0 if touching).

properties.name: _interactive_frame_dims
properties.description: Find frame sizes applied to icon Buttons (Image(systemName:) controls). A frame is "interactive" if, scanning a few lines up the modifier chain, we hit an `Image(systemName:` before a decorative `Circle(`/`Text(`. This keeps the 40x40 send/interrupt icons and rejects the 8x8 status dots that happen to live inside a Button row.

properties.name: _connected_components
properties.description: 4-connectivity flood fill over a 2D boolean block grid (numpy-only).

properties.name: set_content_size
properties.description: Set the simulator's Dynamic Type category. Returns True on success.

properties.name: _app_bg_frac
properties.description: Fraction of pixels close to the app background color (0..1).

properties.name: measure_first_frame
properties.description: Poll screenshots until the app's background dominates the screen. Returns elapsed ms from launch, or None. Includes screenshot-capture latency, so treat it as a harness-relative (but consistent) measure.

properties.name: seed_and_launch
properties.description: Install fresh, seed the credential, cold-launch, and (best-effort) time it. Returns a runtime metrics dict in the reward/scorers/perf.py schema, or {} when nothing could be measured. The uninstall/install makes every launch a true cold launch, so the timing is comparable across cells.

properties.name: device_scale
properties.description: Device pixels per point. SE/mini-class phones and iPads are 2x.

properties.name: _split_top_level
properties.description: Split a brace-group body on top-level commas (ignoring nested braces).

properties.name: _module_imports
properties.description: Parse `use crate::...;` statements in `joined` source text. Returns (group_edge_counts, alias_set): * group_edge_counts: target module -> number of grouped-import references that `CRATE_RE` cannot see (because `{` immediately follows `crate::`). Non-grouped `use crate::name...;` imports are intentionally left to `CRATE_RE` so we never double count. * alias_set: module names brought into local scope as a bare `name::` path prefix (so later bare `name::` usages can be attributed).

properties.name: top_level_modules
properties.description: Return {module_name: [file paths]} for each top-level module. A module `foo` may be backed by `src/foo.rs`, `src/foo/` (dir), or BOTH (a facade `foo.rs` that re-exports a crate plus a small local `foo/` submodule). We collect all backing files under one logical module and remember the canonical entry file (the `.rs` sibling, else `foo/mod.rs`).

properties.name: facade_ratio
properties.description: Return (re-export ratio, facade_lines, code_lines) for the entry file. A high ratio means the module's public surface mostly lives in a crate already; a low ratio means real local logic still lives in the root crate.

properties.name: classify_facade
properties.description: fully | thick | none. fully: entry is essentially just re-exports (already a crate facade). thick: re-exports a crate but keeps a small residual of local API/logic. none: no crate re-export, OR a large module whose bulk still lives locally (a re-export line in mod.rs does not make a 30K-line dir a facade).

properties.name: outbound_refs
properties.description: Return (ref_set, ref_counts) for `crate::<mod>` references. For crate-split planning we care about the *library* dependency graph, so by default we skip test-only files (`*_tests.rs`, `tests.rs`) and lines guarded by an immediately-preceding `#[cfg(test)]`. Test deps would become dev-dependencies and do not constrain how the lib is split into crates. ref_counts maps target module -> number of referencing lines, used as an edge weight: a cheap edge (few references) is easy to invert/cut to break a cycle.

properties.name: strongly_connected_components
properties.description: Tarjan's SCC over the module dependency graph. A component with >1 node (or a self-loop) is a dependency cycle: those modules cannot be split into separate crates without first breaking the cycle (e.g. by extracting a shared trait/interface crate). Returned in reverse-topological order (leaves first).

properties.name: eades_order
properties.description: Eades-Lin-Smyth greedy heuristic returning a vertex order that minimizes backward edges (an approximate minimum feedback arc set).

properties.name: first_int
properties.description: Return the first present integer value among candidate key names.

properties.name: select_latest_instances
properties.description: Keep one coherent process lifetime per target. Daily JSONL files contain multiple server reloads and client processes. PSS deltas across process boundaries are meaningless and previously produced multi-gigabyte false spikes. The default report now follows the latest instance for each target; --all-instances preserves the old forensic view.

properties.name: build_coverage_report
properties.description: Decompose PSS into attributed live, unattributed live heap, allocator retention, file-backed, and stack buckets. Uses allocator stats (mallinfo2/jemalloc) plus the newer smaps_rollup and process_diagnostics fields when present; older logs degrade gracefully to whatever fields exist. The key outputs are two coverage ratios: - coverage_ratio_pss: attributed / PSS (the historical, misleading one; the denominator includes allocator retention and file maps). - coverage_ratio_live_heap: attributed / allocator live bytes (estimator quality against the memory the app actually holds). Explained PSS follows the in-binary summary definition: total_attributed + allocator_retained_resident_estimate + pss_file + thread_stack_estimate.

properties.name: ConnectionPhase
properties.description: Connection lifecycle reported to the UI.

properties.name: ConnectionOutput
properties.description: Everything the UI observes from a connection: lifecycle changes plus decoded server events.

properties.name: Connection
properties.description: Actor owning one WebSocket connection to a jcode server. properties.name: start
properties.description: Starts the connection loop. The returned stream yields phase changes and decoded events until `stop()` is called or the stream is cancelled.

properties.name: send

properties.name: ServerCredential

Falls back to a JSON file in Application Support when the keychain is unavailable (e.g. unsigned simulator builds returning `errSecMissingEntitlement`). Real signed builds use the keychain.

properties.name: InMemoryCredentialStore
properties.description: In-memory store for tests and previews.

properties.name: Gateway
properties.description: Describes a jcode server gateway endpoint. The server exposes: - `GET http://host:port/health` reachability + version probe - `POST http://host:port/pair` pairing-code -> auth-token exchange - `ws://host:port/ws` newline-delimited JSON protocol over WebSocket

properties.name: PairURI
properties.description: Parses `jcode://pair?host=H&port=P&code=C` URIs from QR codes.

properties.name: PairingClient
properties.description: Exchanges a pairing code for a long-lived auth token via `POST /pair`.

properties.name: checkHealth
properties.description: Probes `GET /health`. Returns true when the gateway is reachable.

properties.name: TranscriptEntry
properties.description: One entry in the rendered transcript.

properties.name: Notice

properties.name: SessionState
properties.description: Full client-side session state derived from server events.

properties.name: title
properties.description: Human title for a session in the list, falling back to nil when unknown.

properties.name: LocalIntent
properties.description: Local intents that mutate state without a server round-trip.

properties.name: SessionReducer
properties.description: Pure state machine turning connection output into session state. All streaming, tool lifecycle, and history-sync behavior lives here so it can be exhaustively unit tested on macOS without UI or network.

properties.name: resolvePendingInterrupt
properties.description: Marks the matching queued soft-interrupt as delivered. If the injection came from another client (no optimistic bubble), appends the content so the transcript still reflects what the agent saw.

properties.name: drainPendingInterrupts
properties.description: The turn is over: anything still marked queued has either been consumed server-side or is moot, so stop showing it as pending.

properties.name: withStreamingAssistant
properties.description: Mutates the trailing streaming assistant entry, creating it if needed.

properties.name: WebSocketTransport
properties.description: Abstraction over a WebSocket so `Connection` is testable with a fake.

properties.name: connect
properties.description: Opens the socket. Throws if the connection or auth fails.

properties.name: send
properties.description: Sends one text frame.

properties.name: receiveText
properties.description: Receives the next text frame. Returns nil when the socket closes.

properties.name: close
properties.description: Closes the socket.

properties.name: URLSessionWebSocketTransport
properties.description: URLSession-backed transport used in production. Auth is sent via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on the upgrade request, matching the gateway's preferred auth source.

properties.name: Request
properties.description: Client request to a jcode server. Wire format mirrors `crates/jcode-protocol/src/wire.rs` (`#[serde(tag = "type")]`, snake_case tags). Only the requests the iOS app uses are modeled; the server ignores fields it does not expect.

properties.name: encodedLine
properties.description: Encodes the request as a single JSON line (no trailing newline).

properties.name: ToolCallRecord
properties.description: A tool call as represented in history payloads.

properties.name: HistoryMessage
properties.description: A message in conversation history (response to `get_history`).

properties.name: ServerEvent
properties.description: Server event from a jcode server. Unknown event types decode as `.unknown` so newer servers never break older apps.

properties.name: decode
properties.description: Decodes one newline-delimited JSON event line.

properties.name: JSONObject
properties.description: Lenient JSON accessor. The wire protocol omits absent optionals and the app must never crash on a server that is newer or older than itself.

properties.name: AppModel
properties.description: Observable glue between JCodeKit and the SwiftUI views. Owns the credential store, the active `Connection`, and the derived `SessionState`. Contains no protocol or state-transition logic itself; everything flows through `SessionReducer`.

properties.name: retryConnection
properties.description: Reconnects to the active server without discarding the rendered transcript; the history resync replaces it once the socket is back.

properties.name: compactConversation
properties.description: Asks the server to compact the conversation context.

properties.name: clearConversation
properties.description: Clears the current conversation on the server and optimistically locally.

properties.name: cancelQueuedInterrupts

Ordering is preserved within each session; no total ordering across sessions is claimed. Calling `return()`, aborting `signal`, or closing this client closes every child connection. Custom transports are rejected because the SDK cannot safely clone an arbitrary transport into independent session connections.

properties.description: Explicitly pin the daemon's shared-server channel to an installed build. Promotion and reload intentionally remain separate operations: updates may advance a shared server that tracks stable, but must not overwrite a build the user deliberately promoted here.

properties.name: run_server_reload_command
properties.description: Gracefully reload the running background server onto the newest binary. This is the preferred upgrade path (issue #291): instead of killing the daemon and dropping live headless/swarm sessions, we ask it to hand its sessions off to a freshly exec'd server (the same path `/reload` uses). Behavior: - With `force == false` (the default), the server only reloads when it is provably running older code than an available reload candidate. A server already on the newest binary reports "already up to date" and does nothing, which keeps an installer from downgrading a newer/dev daemon or re-entering the reload-loop family (#277). - With `force == true`, the server reloads unconditionally. - If no server is running, this is a successful no-op so installers can call it unconditionally.

properties.name: run_server_stop_command
properties.description: Stop the running background server gracefully and clear its socket. Intended for use after an upgrade so the next launch starts the freshly installed binary instead of a surviving daemon running old code (issue #291). Steps: 1. Look up the daemon owning the active socket in the server registry and send it SIGTERM (the daemon has a graceful SIGTERM handler). 2. Wait for the listener to go away (bounded), escalating to SIGKILL only if the process refuses to exit. 3. Reap any leftover stale socket so a later launch binds cleanly.

properties.name: run_command_mcp_enabled
properties.description: Whether headless `blaude run` should load MCP servers from `~/.jcode/mcp.json`. Enabled by default; set `JCODE_RUN_MCP=0` (or `false`/`off`/`no`) to skip MCP registration for latency-sensitive scripting. (#390)

properties.name: run_command_mcp_cold_wait

properties.name: cold_cache_mcp_servers
properties.description: Returns the set of MCP servers configured for this run that have no usable cached schema yet (cold cache). Advertise-early can only pre-register tools for servers whose schemas are cached, so these are the servers whose tools would otherwise miss the single-turn snapshot.

properties.name: wait_for_cold_cache_mcp_tools

properties.name: take_run_gate_digest

properties.description: Consume the observation log only once the turn has actually ended. `take_run_gate_digest` clears the log, so calling it while todos are still open would destroy the reminder: auto-poke iterates many times with open work on a long run, and the incomplete-todo follow-up takes precedence, so the digest string would be dropped on the floor with the log already emptied.

properties.description: Human-readable one-line summary used for `--once` and the menu header.

properties.name: SingletonLock
properties.description: A held singleton lock for the menu bar helper. Keeps the lock file open for the whole process lifetime; the kernel releases the advisory lock automatically when the process exits (including via `terminate:`).

properties.name: acquire_singleton_lock
properties.description: Acquire the exclusive, system-wide "only one menu bar helper" lock. Uses a non-blocking `flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` on the *global* `~/.jcode/menubar.lock` (see [`super::global_menubar_dir`]) so the lock is shared across every blaude process for this OS user, including ones running with a sandboxed `$JCODE_HOME`. The menu bar itself is a single per-login-session resource, so the guard must be global too. Returns `Some(guard)` if we are the sole helper, or `None` if another live helper already holds the lock (in which case the caller should exit without creating a second status item). On any unexpected error we fall back to `Some` so a transient filesystem issue never permanently hides the indicator.

properties.name: dummy_file
properties.description: Open `/dev/null` as a stand-in lock handle for the rare case where the real lock file cannot be created. Returns `None` only if even that fails, in which case the caller proceeds without a guard.

properties.name: launch_jcode_window
properties.description: Launch a blaude window off the main thread so slow terminal startup (osascript / `open`) never blocks the menu bar UI.

properties.name: sync_app_appearance
properties.description: Pin the application's appearance to the system Light/Dark setting. `blaude` runs as a bare executable without an `Info.plist` app bundle, so AppKit defaults the process to the light `Aqua` appearance and does not follow the user's macOS Dark Mode preference. With a light appearance the status item's template SF Symbol and `labelColor` title both resolve to a dark/black color, which is invisible against a dark menu bar. Reading `AppleInterfaceStyle` (absent => Light, "Dark" => Dark) and applying the matching named appearance makes those dynamic colors and template images render with proper contrast on whatever menu bar the user has. Safe to call repeatedly; setting the same appearance is a no-op.

properties.name: streaming_color
properties.description: Color used for the count (and icon tint) while any session is actively streaming a response. A slightly muted system green that reads well in both light and dark menu bars.

properties.name: attributed_title
properties.description: Build the colored menu bar title. While streaming, the count is drawn in the streaming color; when idle it uses the primary dynamic label color so it keeps full contrast against whatever the menu bar background is. (The previous secondary/"quiet" gray was nearly invisible on a black/dark menu bar.) `labelColor` is a dynamic system color, so AppKit resolves it at draw time using the status item button's effective appearance - white-ish on a dark menu bar, dark on a light one. The monospaced-digit font is applied so the width stays stable.
